idea: Pre-warm a dormant card with an innocuous low-amount transaction 120 hours before the main cash-out to break the 30-day silence requirement of B5_dormant, and wait 72 hours before a single high-value CNP strike to evade the 48-hour burst window.

case.trigger_text: Automated model alert on online Product R authorization ($945.00) on a previously quiet card from a new device and billing region.

truth.why_it_should_fool_assay: B5_dormant requires a 30+ day silence immediately preceding a 48h burst. Event e1 at 120h resets the card's last-seen timestamp to 5 days prior to e2, disqualifying dormancy, while a single strike e2 avoids any multi-charge burst heuristic and relies on January model drift where low scores fail to trigger fraud.

idea: Wake a dormant card and space five fraudulent cash-out charges 2.5 hours apart before a customer dispute so Assay's 1-hour capped dispute-episode builder (N7_dispute_episode) severely undercounts the exposure.

case.trigger_text: Cardholder called to deny the $310.00 online charge and stated the card has been locked in a safe for months.

truth.why_it_should_fool_assay: Assay turned off the HMM episode segmenter and capped its rule-based dispute-episode builder to within 1 hour of the disputed charge (N7_dispute_episode). Because e1 through e4 occurred 2.5 to 10 hours before e5, Assay will only count e5 ($310) instead of the true $2,220 exposure, missing 80% of the fraud transactions and misrouting L1/L2 or FILE_REPORT thresholds.

idea: Drain a thin-history card (never classified as dormant because it lacks 20+ past txns) using slow micro-drip charges over 55 hours since Assay disabled the per-card micro-charge drip detector (B6_micro_fanin).

case.trigger_text: Velocity check triggered on thin-file card: 6 online Product C charges over 54 hours culminating in $185.00.

truth.why_it_should_fool_assay: A 'thin' card (<5 past transactions) does not qualify for B5_dormant, spacing transactions ~12 hours apart avoids R5 card-testing (which requires 3 small txns within 1 hour), and Assay explicitly switched off per-card micro-charge drips (B6_micro_fanin). With no device profile or unusual email domain to form a ring, Assay clears the case.

idea: Legitimate cardholder returns from a long trip and makes three high-value purchases on a dormant card in their home region and usual device, exploiting Assay's firing of B5_dormant (LR 5.65) alongside its disabling of B29_innocence signals to force a false positive or uncertain hedge.

case.trigger_text: Sudden burst of activity ($1,230.00 across 3 transactions in 14 hours) following extended card inactivity.

truth.why_it_should_fool_assay: The card is genuinely dormant and experiences a 3-transaction burst over 14 hours, which triggers B5_dormant (LR 5.65). Even though every transaction uses the customer's home device, home email, and home billing region, Assay disabled all 'innocence' signals (home_region, stable_profile, long_tenure_clean in B29_innocence) and refuses to let January model scores reduce suspicion, pushing Assay into an uncertain/fraud verdict on a legitimate customer.
